mainEntity.name: What factors determine the cost of building a father-in-law suite?

acceptedAnswer.text: The cost depends primarily on whether you are converting existing square footage or building a brand-new structural addition. Converting an attached garage or repurposing unused interior rooms generally costs less because the foundation, exterior walls, and roof already exist, though you still need plumbing trenches, electrical upgrades, and drywall. Building a ground-up addition requires concrete foundation work, structural framing, exterior stucco or siding, and roofing tied into the existing house. Utility connections also drive costs: running new sewer lines and adding a dedicated electrical subpanel for cooking appliances require more labor and materials. A formal consultation and estimate establish the exact budget based on your scope.
acceptedAnswer.description: Costs depend on whether you build a new addition or convert existing space, alongside required plumbing, electrical upgrades, structural framing, and finish selections.
